data.narrative:
Augury is a Series F robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz that has raised $369M to date. The target operates within a sector comprising one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Locus Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Of the two valuation methods applied, only stage-progression proved actionable. This method uses the $369M total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical for Series F progression to successor financing rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $480M. A peer-median approach was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables: while ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, fewer than three met simultaneous filters for stage, stage-adjacency, or valuation tier, making sector-wide median benchmarking potentially misleading.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $408M (low) to $552M (median $480M), anchored entirely on the stage-progression method. The substantial range reflects limited comparable datapoints and the inherent uncertainty in applying standard step-up multiples to a frontier-stage company. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, technology defensibility within the manufacturing software space, and path to profitability—factors not captured by mechanics-based progression alone. Additional transaction data or narrowing of the peer set would materially sharpen this range.
